speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: asked the Minister for Health whether he can provide an update on the war against diabetes and how successful has the Ministry been in the preventive, reactive and research programmes in diabetes prevention and management since the programme began.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The War on Diabetes was launched in 2016 to mobilise the whole nation to tackle diabetes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Since then, we have made encouraging progress across prevention, early detection and management of the disease, but much more remains to be done.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For more effective prevention, we need to tackle risk factors, such as unhealthy diets and inactive lifestyles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: To encourage food manufacturers to innovate and reformulate to produce healthier alternatives, HPB has extended the Healthier Ingredient Development Scheme in 2018 to three additional product categories, namely, sugar-sweetened beverages, desserts and sauces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: There are early indications that these efforts are producing some results.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For example, more Singaporeans are becoming more physically active.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: More than 800,000 Singaporeans participated in Season 4 of HPB's National Steps Challenge, four times that in Season 1.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Based on the 2018 National Nutrition Survey, our diet quality has also improved.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Unsaturated fat is displacing saturated fat, which has decreased to 36% of total fat consumed in 2018 from 38% in 2010.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: However, sugar and salt intakes are still causes for concern.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The average daily salt intake was nine gm in 2018, with 90% of Singaporeans exceeding the recommended intake of five gm per day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In November 2018, the Government decided to form a HealthySG Taskforce to further promote healthy living and activate the community to support the efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The HealthySG Taskforce has recommended several initiatives, including the adoption of technology-enabled, personalised coaching solutions and a lifelong virtual Health Booklet for individuals to track their personal health status.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will also implement a support programme for lower-income families to help them stay healthy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Early detection of diabetes is important, and we encourage Singaporeans to go for regular, age-appropriate screening and follow-up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: To make screening more convenient, the Ministry of Health (MOH) has enhanced the Screen for Life (SFL) Programme and recently adopted non-fasting tests which facilitate opportunistic screening.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: More than 65,000 Singaporeans have benefited from cardiovascular and cancer screening in the 18 months following the enhancement of SFL subsidies in September 2017.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This is almost 30 times higher than the number of Singaporeans who have come forward for screening over the preceding 18 months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We have also made efforts to enhance the management of diabetes and reduce related complications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For example, we formulated a national strategy to reduce lower extremity amputations among diabetic patients through timely detection and clinical management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: More recently, MOH issued an Appropriate Care Guide on foot assessment in people with diabetes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These guidelines help healthcare professionals better perform comprehensive foot assessment and treat diabetic complications in a timely manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We have also been conducting more local research to understand the effectiveness and impact of our interventions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For instance, Pre-Diabetes Interventions and Continued Tracking to Ease out Diabetes (Pre-DICTED) is a research programme by SingHealth to evaluate the effectiveness of a community-based intervention programme in reducing the conversion rate from pre-diabetes to diabetes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Data from this study can help us develop evidence-based, scalable and effective interventions for better clinical management and policies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: While there are early signs of progress in our war against diabetes, we cannot afford to let up our efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Many of these initiatives will only achieve the desired health outcomes in the long term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Government will continue to work with key stakeholders and partners in the public, private and people sectors to sustain our efforts in this war.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I am aware that in Khoo Teck Puat Hospital, there is actually a group of clinicians who have done quite a bit of very good work in the research into prevention and better management of diabetes cases.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I am suggesting whether MOH can consider whether our public healthcare clusters, possibly in partnership with the Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine or Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine, to develop a dedicated research centre, to look into areas to better prevent, manage, overcome and also win the war against diabetes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, I agree with the Member that research is important to inform clinical management and policies as well as for an effective war on diabetes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Currently, there is a fair amount of collaboration among researchers and clinicians within and across the healthcare, academic and research institutions on diabetes with funding from various sources since the war on diabetes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This includes the Growing Up in Singapore Towards Healthy Outcomes study which is a collaboration among the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), the KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital, the National University Health System and the National University of Singapore (NUS) as well as the Pre-DICTED study that I mentioned earlier, which is between SingHealth Duke-NUS Diabetes Centre with HPB and the Singapore Clinical Research Institute.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, I think that because there is currently sufficient research focus on disease management locally, both in small and large scale research, a current-state mapping of the research landscape for diabetes will need to be done to understand the range of research that has already been funded, and to ensure that the full potential of any research centre to be set up could be achieved without significant overlaps, especially with the large scale research projects that have already been funded.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Also, as the researchers for these projects often come from multiple organisations, such as academia as well as the healthcare clusters and so on, actually we could take this to be akin to a virtual centre for diabetes research, which tap on the best researchers from Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Nonetheless, we will further study the Member's suggestion and see how useful and appropriate such a dedicated research centre would be.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Just two supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I just wanted to ask whether the Ministry has any ideas to perhaps increase either subsidies or further funding support for patients with diabetes.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Just to give an example, diabetes is part of the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP) but not all of the chronic diseases are created equal.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, I was wondering since we have this war against diabetes, whether we could look at some package where there could be additional funding liberated either from patients' MediSave or, perhaps from other targeted subsidies for patients with diabetes, because this would probably help to increase compliance.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The second supplementary question is related to my later question, but I think I will just ask it here.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We are all concerned to see that the sugar intake per day of Singaporeans, as of a survey last year, is still at 60 grammes, and the World Health Organization's (WHO's) standard is 25 grammes every day.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, I was wondering whether MOH has any targets.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Have we set any targets for the sugar intake per day for Singaporeans, and do we have any timeline to try and reach these targets?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That means that they can claim on MediSave and it also goes under CDMP, through the Community Health Assist Scheme funding, for instance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, as with healthcare affordability issues, the Ministry will continue to look into ensuring the affordability of treatment and access for the different conditions, including for diabetes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will review the feedback and also take into account evidence from local and regional studies and then make our decision.
